name: base-tokenizedstocks-docs
what_this_is: An address book of primary documentation for tokenized equity on Base. It is not the skill itself — SKILL.md holds the frameworks; this file tells the agent which official docs exist, which URL to open, and which analysis each source serves. Do not ingest the whole list into context: identify the issuer or data need under analysis, then fetch only the matching rows. Liveness verified 2026-09-06. Re-verify any row on first use in a session.
how_to_use: Identify what the question needs: issuer terms (Dinari, Coinbase, Backed), the token standard (B20), or market data (price, dividends).
Select rows whose category and skill_use match that need. Cap at 3 to 4 fetches per answer.
Dinari docs serve raw markdown: append .md to any page URL for a fetch-friendly version, and docs.dinari.com/llms.txt indexes the full site.
Treat issuer docs as claims until cross-checked: a promised dividend pass-through is terms-only evidence until a live event has exercised it.

Issuer status is a first-class fact. Dinari actively issues (714 dShares, 2026-09-06 count); Coinbase actively issues B20 stocks (13 tickers as of 2026-09-08 registry, ex-US); Backed is redemption-only. The token set is session-derived from the registry when precision matters — the counts here are dated snapshots, not the ceiling. An answer that treats them interchangeably is wrong.

The skill's subject is Base exclusively. Off-Base rows (xstocks, ondo-stocks) exist for mechanism comparison and print evidence about the class — never as an analysis subject, venue, or recommendation.
When analyzing a specific token, always pair the issuer row with the B20 standard row — eligibility enforcement lives in the standard's policy scopes, not in the issuer's marketing.

priority_legend.must: Fetch whenever the analysis touches this issuer or primitive. Answers are wrong without it.
priority_legend.core: Fetch when that name or its product is under review.
priority_legend.should: Add when the question expands beyond the core loop.
priority_legend.thin: Weak or gated public docs. Use as a pointer, not as a source of truth.

sources.name: Dinari dShares
sources.skill_use: Primary active issuer for the claim stack: what a dShare legally is, how dividends reach holders, how splits/ticker changes/mergers are processed, who may hold per jurisdiction, and which chains carry the tokens (Base confirmed, eip155:8453). 714 dShares listed as of 2026-09-06. Dedicated pages define the split rebase mechanics (halt-rebase-verify-resume, paused while IN_PROGRESS, fractions liquidated to USD+) and merger outcomes per consideration type (manual triage, no endpoint — a disappearing position is the signal). Custody, brokerage, and compliance are handled by Dinari under the hood. The Base dividend pipe is staged, not exercised: the DividendDistribution contract on Base (0x7978c49C4861e43692702FD74b12B620eE47601e) has executed five transactions lifetime — deployment, a role grant, a 2025-09-18 test createDistribution (0.78 USD+) of which 0.77 paid to a Dinari-affiliated wallet holding nearly all that test token's supply, and a 2026-02-04 reclaim — and Dinari's deployment registry tags the Base entry staging (production distributions: Plume). Docs drift: two USD+ contracts exist on Base and usdplus-evm.md lists the one the distribution contract has never paid from. Verified 2026-09-07 via tx records and Basescan.

sources.name: Backed bTokens
sources.skill_use: A retired product line, not a dead issuer: Backed was acquired by Kraken (announced 2025-12-02) and went all-in on xStocks in March 2026 (Solana — off-Base); the 17 bTokens (bNVDA CH1173294336, bTSLA, bCOIN, bMSFT, and bond/ETF trackers) remain redeemable for existing holders but closed to new issuance as of 2026-09-06. Use for claim-stack comparisons against an active issuer, as the candidate pool for underlying-level corporate-action prints, and as the class's only issuer-level print to date — an acquisition-pivot that closed issuance while leaving redemption open. Each product page carries an ISIN — the traceable legal identifier of the underlying wrapper.

sources.name: xStocks (Backed × Kraken)
sources.skill_use: Backed's active product line post-pivot (March 2026): tokenized equities on Solana and EVM chains, distributed with Kraken. Corporate actions run through an onchain multiplier that accumulates over the token's life: dividends are reinvested rather than distributed ('net of applicable withholding taxes'), splits scale the multiplier up, reverse splits scale it down, activation lands 00:30 UTC the day after the ex-date (observed 23:55–04:00), and holders never act. Chain implementations differ — EVM contracts rebase balances directly; on Solana and TON the onchain balance stays constant with the multiplier in token metadata, so a balance-history check shows nothing there. Print VERIFIED 2026-09-07, the class's first for an underlying-level dividend: the issuer API's dated activation log cross-checked onchain to full precision — AAPLx moved 1.0 → 1.0033 through five quarterly dividend activations (2025-08-14 to 2026-08-08, Solana and the identically-valued Ethereum contract), SPYx 1.0 → 1.0057 through four (2025-10-31 to 2026-06-18); the contract's event counter equals the log length. Per-issuer evidence: this proves xStocks' reinvestment pipe and nothing about Dinari's USD+ distribution on Base. Reads: api.xstocks.fi/api/v2/public/assets/{SYMBOL}/multiplier[/history]?network={NETWORK} (keyless; the multiplier-history route in api-routes.json), EVM eth_call getCurrentMultiplier() (multiplier as 1e18 mantissa; one contract address reused across all EVM deployments; no Base deployment exists), Solana metadata extension on Solscan. Off-Base: mechanism comparison and print evidence only, never a Base example. Docs pulled via curl with a browser user-agent on 2026-09-07 (plain automated fetch gets 403).

sources.name: B20 Token Standard (Base)
sources.skill_use: The token standard tokenized equity deploys through on Base — and it carries the dividend mechanism itself, not just plumbing: corporate actions and dividends adjust a single multiplier ('cash dividends are converted to shares of the underlying equity and reflected via a multiplier update... rather than distributed as cash'), so one B20 token does not permanently equal one share, and every conversion between tokens and shares applies the current multiplier. Onchain reads: multiplier() (WAD 1e18), scaledBalanceOf(address), toScaledBalance/toRawBalance; history in MultiplierUpdated events, scheduled changes via updateUIMultiplier with advance onchain notice. Policy scopes (allowlist/blocklist transfer control), pausing, seizure, and supply caps remain the eligibility-enforcement layer at the contract. Verified 2026-09-07: all 13 live B20 tokens read multiplier exactly 1.0 — the mechanism is terms-only, never exercised.

sources.name: Coinbase Tokenized Stocks (B20)
sources.skill_use: The second live issuer on Base (verified 2026-09-07): Coinbase-issued B20 tokenized stocks, 'backed 1:1 by shares held in regulated custody' — each token 'a beneficial claim on a real share, held in regulated, bankruptcy-remote custody separate from Coinbase'. The issuing entity is Coinbase Onchain SPV Ltd, with ADGM prospectus documents linked per token on base.org/stocks (read 2026-09-08). 13 live tokens as of the 2026-09-08 registry (NVDAc, METAc, AAPLc, GOOGLc, AMZNc, MSFTc, MSTRc, SNDKc, SPCXc, TSLAc, COINc, CRCLc, INTCc), full addresses in the docs page (onchain registry 0x3f3E8cf41cdd3b1D118c16471aB0113DfDDd5CaD) — re-read the registry per session; the count is a snapshot, not the ceiling. Eligible jurisdictions outside the US only; mint/redeem restricted to KYC'd Authorized Participants, secondary trading permissionless. Dividends and splits run through the B20 multiplier (b20-standard row) — the issuer's own stocks page asks 'How are dividends and splits handled?' and publishes no answer, and all registry multipliers read exactly 1.0 on 2026-09-07: terms-only (re-sweep via route b20-multiplier). The page's partner list (Aave, Morpho, Euler, Beefy, Glider, Virtuals, and more) is a tagline surface — verify a named venue and contract before treating any entry as live (Beefy vaults verified live; a same-day Morpho spot-check found no live stock market). The 2026-08-24 launch announcement names the custody chain: Authorized Participants buy the shares, which go to Alpaca, a regulated broker and custodian, in a bankruptcy-remote structure supervised by Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) regulators; once minted the tokens are standard B20 — 'no whitelisted wallets and no platform lock-in'. Which B20 trade in live pools against USDC is a session-derived set (registry enumeration + token-price route); on 2026-09-08 the snapshot read only 4 — NVDAc, GOOGLc, AAPLc, METAc (docs.basestonk.io/stock-pairs.md) — and more have gone live since. An empty pool enumeration is a finding about where the market lives, not an absence of product — state it dated, per token.

sources.name: Base B20 Ecosystem Announcement
sources.skill_use: Base's official B20 launch announcement ('Stocks just got updated.', published 2026-08-24) and the closest thing to an official ecosystem directory: it names every third-party protocol that 'publicly announced support for the B20 standard' (list transcribed from the article's ecosystem graphic, 2026-09-07). DEX: Aerodrome. Trading venues: Signa, SOSOValue, Virtuals, Maestro, Definitive, Tribeca, Banana Gun, Wasabi, 01 Exchange, bankr, Flaunch, Treasure, True Markets. Aggregators: Li.Fi, 0x, CoW Swap, Beefy, 1inch, KyberSwap, Portals, Matcha, Jumper. Borrow/lend: Aave, Morpho, Euler. Portfolio: Reserve, Glider, ZyfAI, Enso. Wallets: Base App, Bitget Wallet, OKX Wallet, Fomo. Curators: Bitwise, Dialectic, Clearstar, Steakhouse, Tau Labs, Gauntlet. Neobanks: Superform, Avici, ample.money, Liminal Cash, defi.com. Fintech: Fusion, Grow, Zoth, Makina, Castar, Centrifuge. Oracle: Chainlink. TWO USES: (1) launchpad identity resolution for the meme/stock genre — the dex ids 'o1-launchpad' and 'bankr' in pool data correspond to 01 Exchange and bankr, both named here as trading venues; Flaunch is the other named launchpad. (2) The tagline-versus-venue sweep list: announced support is a claim, not a live market — verify venue and contract before treating any entry as real (Morpho named here, yet the 2026-09-07 spot-check found no live stock market; Beefy named and verified live). Direct fetch 403s (bot protection); read via a reader proxy or search cache. Names the custodian too (see coinbase-stocks row).

sources.name: Base Token Launchpads (o1, bankr, Flaunch)
sources.skill_use: The launchpad layer for the meme/stock genre (meme-pair-launchpad.md, factory layer). Three venues, named in Base's official B20 ecosystem announcement (base-b20-ecosystem row) with homepages and docs verified reachable 2026-09-07: o1 — o1.exchange ('Trading Terminal on Base/Solana', docs 'Democratizing Alpha for Traders'); this is the dex id 'o1-launchpad' that dominates the meme/stock pools on Base. bankr — bankr.bot (AI-agent trading surface: buy/sell/swap, limit orders) plus docs. Flaunch — flaunch.gg ('Launch. Trade. Earn.'), docs live; named by Base but not yet seen in the genre's pool data. USE: when a pool's dex identifies its launchpad, resolve the venue here, then demand the launch mechanics from that venue's docs — hook permissions, fee control, liquidity locking — before any fairness claim; the docs' depth is itself a signal (a launchpad with no documented hook permissions is a hook you are trusting blind). Homepages verified reachable; deep mechanics pages not yet audited — re-verify on first use.

sources.name: BaseStonk Launchpad
sources.skill_use: A Base launchpad NOT named in Base's official B20 ecosystem announcement (found by the user, 2026-09-07) — proof the official list is non-exhaustive. One transaction creates a token, its Uniswap v4 pool and trading from block one: no bonding curve, no graduation, no migration; the launcher must end every launch holding nothing; no admin key over any pool; current generation V6 (AdvancedLauncherV6 + AdvancedFeeHookV6, source-verified addresses in the contracts page), with a separate B20 rail (AdvancedLauncherB20V6) for launches against native B20 tokens. Its Pairs page is the cleanest map of the stock-leg landscape on Base: three kinds — (1) native Coinbase B20 (per their docs only four tokens trade in live pools); (2) the ST0x wrapped family, eleven 1:1-backed equities/ETFs with real DEX liquidity (wtCOIN, wtNVDA, wtMSTR, wtSPCX + wtSGOV/wtSKHY/wtSPYM/wtDRAM/wtQQQM/wtIAU/wtCEG; wtCOIN verified onchain at 0x5cDa0E1CA4ce2af96315f7F8963C85399c172204, supply ~1,343) — a separate claim stack from the registry tokens, walk the wrapper's backing before treating it as the share; (3) Robinhood Chain's own 194 stocks (chain 4663 side; off-Base evidence). The same Pairs page (2026-09-08) documents the live-market state of Coinbase B20 tokens: only four of thirteen trade in live pools against USDC (NVDAc, GOOGLc, AAPLc, METAc) — the other nine have no onchain market yet, so ETH cannot route into them; an empty pool enumeration for those nine is a finding, not an absence of product. Chainlink equity feeds refuse beyond 96h staleness ('24h would fail every Saturday') — a venue admitting the two-clock problem the onchain-basis rubric is built on. wtNVDA (0xfb5b41acdba20a3230f84be995173cfb98b8d6e7, verified onchain 2026-09-08) is the NVIDIA leg of the ST0x family — Chainlink-priced, ~5 DEX books, ~$14k total reserve; a direct NVDAc/wtNVDA 0.05% pool on hydrex-integral (created 2026-08-26, $4.1k reserve) is a live market whose subject is the native-vs-wrapper spread. Keyless REST API at api.basestonk.io (per-launch hook, generation, pair, pressure). 'Dividend baskets' = trade-fee dividends paid in creator-picked assets, NOT equity dividends — the word collides with the corporate-action rubric's subject; keep the two claims separate. Also operates on Robinhood Chain (deployed 2026-09-04) — that side is evidence, never a venue.
